## Historical audit — S0008

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. The supplied observations contain image paths, not image pixels.

| Stage | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and input | The student was asked to reconstruct a 512 × 341 indoor photograph with separate meshes and a matching camera, without using the photograph as a texture. Its bedroom inventory is an **inference from the reference**, not independent audit observation (student model_request, line 1; model_response, line 3). |
| Initial build | The program created multiple named assets: room, windows, bed, settee, screen, tables, chair, pictures and rugs. Named child primitives describe, for example, bed rails and posts and settee arms and feet; parent membership does not verify physical connections. It assigned colors, procedural wallpaper and window emission, plus camera and lights (student model_response, line 3; execute, line 4). |
| First validation and exploration | Step 1 rendered successfully in 16.66 seconds; the runner selected it and supplied the render to the next student call (execution_result, line 5; select, line 6; model_request, line 7). The student reported excessive ceiling, a short distant bed, a frontal displaced chair, pale lighting and an undersized screen. These are student assessments, not independently verified defects (model_response, line 9). The sessions report no student tool calls; the visible exploration is the build–render–revise loop, not external research (codex_session, lines 2 and 8). |
| Revision and result | The executed revision lengthened the bed, moved and rotated the settee, raised the screen, changed wallpaper shading, reduced lighting, and changed camera lens from 40 to 44 with a revised target (execute, lines 4 and 10). Step 2 succeeded in 18.20 seconds and was selected; its render was supplied for review with no executions remaining. The student responded `DONE` (execution_result, line 11; select, line 12; model_request, line 13; model_response, line 15). |
| Teacher input | No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student receipt appears in this student trajectory. The system’s general instructions and runner’s render-feedback prompt were received, but they are not evidence of a separate teacher intervention (lines 1 and 7). |

**Outcome:** Both builds and renders succeeded technically, and step 2 was selected. Visual or geometric correctness is **unknown**: neither the reference nor renders are visible in the supplied audit text. `DONE`, asset names and successful execution do not establish a match. In particular, object coverage and occlusion, material resemblance, actual part contact, settee pose, camera framing and illumination remain unverified. The student’s first-render diagnoses and the effect of the simultaneous revisions remain hypotheses; no independent comparison establishes improvement or isolates a cause.

**Lessons:** Transferably, a complete initial build followed by rendered feedback enabled a concrete revision within two executions; execution success alone did not validate appearance. Task-specific choices—bed dimensions, settee rotation, wallpaper noise and lighting values—are attempts for this particular inferred bedroom, not general prescriptions. The record does not show a measured final comparison or further correction.
